pr_title: Make Extensions.FileProviders supported in browser and only unsupport FSW usage
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/56178

Since `PhysicalFilesWatcher` can be used without a `FileSystemWatcher` through polling, I reduced the unsupported scenarios to only the ones that actually use FSW in browser with a couple of runtime checks.
Let me know if this is not a good idea and instead we should mark the whole type as unsupported.

issue_context.title: Most of Microsoft.Extensions.FileProviders.Physical should be supported on Browser
issue_context.body:
Hosting uses `PhysicalFileProvider`, which is not supported on Browser. See https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/55664.

We should just mark the specific APIs that aren't supported on Browser instead of the whole assembly.

cc @SteveSandersonMS @pranavkm @Tratcher @davidfowl @Jozkee

Hosting uses `PhysicalFileProvider`, which is not supported on Browser. See https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/55664. We should just make Hosting not supported on Browser, since it is not used. review_comments:
Won't this still throw PNSE when creating a `PhysicalFileProvider` on browser? Shouldn't the logic be something like:


```C#
(UsePollingFileWatcher && UseActivePolling) || OperatingSystem.IsBrowser() ? null : ...
```
Ah I see, so we should always fallback to use polling on browser. That makes sense to me.
Why this method has no annotation?
Same question here, if it throws for browser all time it should have `[UnsupportedOSPlatform("browser")]`?

Because it doesn't throw for browser all the time; it only throws if `fileSystemWatcher` is not null, theoretically, you can still call this .ctor passing a null FileSystemWatcher and with `pollForChanges = true` in browser.

Is there a way to signal that something is not supported if certain parameter is null/not null (similar to [`NotNullIfNotNullAttribute`](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.codeanalysis.notnullifnotnullattribute?view=net-5.0))?
No, we have been talking about that, but there were not many (known) cases to add such option
Well, I think this is one case 😃.
yeah, we might add that in the future
